courses.title: Geography & History of the World
courses.description: The standard social studies requirement for freshmen. Students use geographical skills and historical concepts to deepen their understanding of global themes, using primary and secondary sources to produce maps, timelines, and other graphic representations. Key concepts include change over time, cultural landscape, diffusion, human-environment interactions, physical systems, and spatial organization and variation.

courses.title: Geography & History of the World Honors
courses.description: Serves as an introduction to Advanced Placement social studies courses for freshmen, demanding the academic excellence expected from an AP course including advanced study skills and rigorous out-of-school work. Students use geographical skills and historical concepts to deepen their understanding of global themes, developing non-fiction literacy skills by analyzing primary and secondary sources.

courses.title: Early College Geography & History of the World

prerequisites.note: Accepted admittance into Early College Cohort

courses.description: Part of the Early College curriculum, designed as a college preparatory course with increasing time commitment, rigor, and critical thinking as the year progresses, helping prepare students for future dual credit courses. Taught in tandem with Early College English 9, with some cross-curricular assignments. Uses geographical skills and historical concepts to deepen understanding of global themes.

courses.title: World History & Civilization
courses.description: A year-long course beginning with the Renaissance and ending with the fall of communism, exploring major historical events/perspectives, political systems, changing geographic boundaries, colonialism, industrialization, political revolutions/independence, causes/effects of wars, and globalization. Uses primary/secondary sources, project-based learning, and Canvas activities, requiring active engagement in discussions and coursework.

courses.title: World History AP
special_notes: Students required to take AP exam in May
courses.description: Designed to be the equivalent of a two-semester introductory college world history course, investigating significant events, individuals, developments, and processes from approximately 1200 CE to the present. Students analyze primary and secondary sources, make historical comparisons, and develop historical arguments, writing three long essays per quarter in preparation for the AP exam. Expect 5-7 hours of homework per week.

courses.title: US History
courses.description: A required two-semester course for all juniors, expanding on concepts from prior American History courses and emphasizing national development from the Civil War period through the 21st century. Students study common themes, key events and people, and various movements through primary/secondary sources, internet activities, music, and film, with a focus on evaluating individual performance.

courses.title: US History AP / Dual Credit
special_notes: Recommended: Honors English and/or Honors GHW
Students required to take AP exam in May
courses.description: APUSH is a full-year, rigorous, college-level course exploring United States history from 1491 to the present, designed for students looking to challenge themselves beyond the required US History course. Emphasizes analytical and writing skills through critical evaluation of primary/secondary sources. Also accredited through Vincennes University, granting 6 transferable college credits (HIST 139 and 140) upon passage.

courses.title: US Government
courses.description: Required of all seniors, investigates the mechanics and operation of political institutions, with the role of citizens, the Constitution, history, geography, economics, and cultures as focus areas. Major units include political participation, the role of the courts, the Presidency, the Congress, and civil liberties, with activities like Mock Congress.

courses.title: US Government (We the People) Dual Credit
special_notes: Confirmed by owner as distinct dual-credit code (not same as standard US Government's 1540).
courses.description: Follows the "We the People: The Citizen and the Constitution" curriculum, a one-semester honors course offered in fall that counts toward the required Government credit, intended for college-bound students passionate about politics, history, debate, and civics. Introduces students to constitutional law, how the Constitution came into existence, and how it has functioned over the past two hundred years. Students are required to participate in regional, state, and national competitions, which require dedicating time outside of class.

courses.title: US Government AP / Dual Credit
courses.description: Intended for motivated, college-bound seniors, this comprehensive study of American government prepares students for the rigors of the college classroom. Topics include federalism, theories of the origins and purposes of government, interest groups, political parties, the electoral process, constitutional backgrounds, and the organization of executive, legislative, and judicial branches. Students develop college-level reading, writing, critical thinking, and discussion skills.

courses.title: Economics
special_notes: Not a required base-diploma course under the new Indiana Diploma (unlike the old Core 40).
courses.description: Designed to stimulate students' awareness of and interest in economics, the study of decision making. Individual units apply this to policy problems such as poverty, taxes, pollution, economic growth, money/banking, GDP, prices, and interest rate changes. Students demonstrate understanding through a special project, with other projects developing skills in Personal Finance, Media Literacy, Global Thinking, and Project Planning.

courses.title: Macroeconomics AP
special_notes: Recommended AP US History or AP World History
Students required to take AP exam in May
courses.description: Recommended for highly motivated students planning to major in economics or business in college, using materials and exams from universities nationwide. Students master basic economic problems relative to aggregate demand/supply, economic growth, deficits, debts, interest rates, loans, and international trade. Expect 2-3 hours of homework per week, mostly college-level reading and practice problems.

courses.title: Human Geography AP
special_notes: Recommended: Honors GHW or World History
Students required to take AP exam in May
courses.description: Introduces students to the systematic study of patterns and processes that have shaped human understanding, use, and alteration of Earth's surface, employing spatial concepts and landscape analysis to examine human social organization and environmental consequences. A full-year, college-level, highly project-oriented course requiring 4-6 hours of homework each week including college-level readings and writing.

courses.title: Comparative Government and Politics AP
special_notes: CONFIRMED INACTIVE by owner: FCHS does not offer this course - what they actually offer is United States Government. Excluded from active course list. The 1574/CCGV code initially associated with this entry actually belongs to US Government AP/Dual Credit - corrected there instead.
courses.description: Compares the American governmental system to political systems around the world, focusing on Great Britain, Mexico, Russia, Iran, China, and Nigeria, developing college-level reading, writing, critical thinking, discussion, and note-taking skills. Note: FCHS does not currently offer this course - included here for reference only.

courses.title: Psychology
courses.description: Intended for college-bound students interested in examining the various perspectives in psychology, the scientific study of behavior and mental processes. Utilizes a variety of activities requiring critical thinking, covering the history and background of psychology, research methods, biological bases of behavior, sensation and perception, developmental psychology, cognition, personality, clinical psychology, and social psychology.

courses.title: Psychology AP
special_notes: Students required to take AP exam in May
courses.description: Based on College Board content, designed to be equivalent to an introductory college course, introducing students to the systematic and scientific study of behavior and mental processes. Topics include History and Approaches, Research Methods, Biological Bases of Behavior, Sensation and Perception, States of Consciousness, Learning, Cognition, Motivation and Emotion, Developmental Psychology, Personality, Testing, Clinical Psychology, and Social Psychology.

courses.title: Sociology
courses.description: An introduction to the theories and concepts of sociology, the study of groups, illustrating how the groups you belong to (by choice or assignment) profoundly influence how you think, feel, and act. Major themes include culture, socialization, race and ethnicity, deviance and social control, crime and punishment, inequities of age/gender/class, and the social agents of religion, education, and family.

courses.title: Indiana Studies
courses.description: Highlights the Hoosier people, places, culture, and events, past and present, for students looking to study Indiana history with a deeper, more focused approach through reading, writing, discussion, and mini-projects. Topics covered include Indiana geography, native peoples, immigration, economics, politics, culture, and the role of conflict in shaping Indiana's history.

courses.title: Ethnic Studies
special_notes: CONFIRMED INACTIVE by owner: not on FCHS master schedule for 2026-27. Excluded from active course list.
courses.description: Provides opportunities to broaden students' perspectives concerning cultural, geographical, political, and socioeconomic patterns of ethnic groups in the United States, focusing on the experiences of Indigenous Americans, African Americans, Latinx Americans, and Asian Americans and Pacific Islanders. Note: not currently on FCHS's master schedule - included here for reference only.

courses.title: European History AP

prerequisites.note: Grade 10 students who completed AP World History also eligible

special_notes: Students required to take AP exam in May
courses.description: Explores the impact of Europe from the 1200s to modern day through readings, essays, primary sources, and projects, at a college level requiring heavy reading and writing. Recommended for juniors and seniors prepared for nightly homework in addition to other assignments. Registration requires taking the AP European History exam in May.

courses.title: Law Education
courses.description: Introduces students to the complex topic of the law and how society interacts with it, challenging students to develop knowledge and skills necessary to remedy interpersonal conflict and understand their place within the structure of the law. Involves independent research, cooperative skills, and reading court opinions and legal documents through investigative research projects, mock trials, and guest speaker presentations, culminating in a Moot Court where students argue a case before staff and real attorneys.

courses.title: Personal Financial Literacy
special_notes: NOT YET ACTIVE: starts 2027-28 school year per department guide. Excluded from 2026-27 active course list, kept here for forward reference only.
courses.description: A combined course merging the state-mandated Personal Financial Literacy class with a standard economics course, helping students understand the fundamentals of good personal finance and how the economic system affects their daily lives. Includes projects and assessments focused on real-world applications. Not yet active - starts for the 2027-28 school year.
